content.title: About
content.content: Mirepoix is a classic blend of finely diced vegetables—typically onion, carrot and celery—sautéed until soft. Cooked mirepoix is used as an aromatic base for sauces, soups, stews and many other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional French mixture is named after the town of Mirepoix in Normandy.
Classic ratio: 2 parts onion, 1 part carrot, 1 part celery.
Cooked mirepoix is often sold frozen, preserving flavor and saving prep time.
Variations may include leeks, garlic, bell pepper or tomatoes.
Mirepoix forms the foundation of over 80 % of classic French sauces.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The vegetables provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie flavor enhancer
items.content: Mirepoix adds depth of taste without significantly increasing a dish’s calorie count.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Onion, carrot and celery supply vitamin C, vitamin K, folate and potassium.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and flavonoids from onions act as antioxidants.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: The combination of vitamins and phytochemicals helps bolster the immune system.

items.title: Celery allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to celery, a component of mirepoix.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared product
items.content: Frozen cooked mirepoix can contain added salt; people with hypertension should check the label.

items.title: Nutrient loss during long storage
items.content: Extended freezing may reduce vitamin C levels.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add the cooked mirepoix to a hot pan with a little oil, sauté 5‑7 minutes until golden, then continue with the main recipe. It works well in béchamel, tomato sauces, soups, stews, risotto and meat dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen mirepoix in an airtight bag at –18 °C. After thawing, use within 2‑3 days and store in the refrigerator in a sealed container. Discard if any off‑odors develop.
